title: Event log and debugging
goal: Diagnose a defect using safe logs, a debugger and a reproducible scenario.
prerequisites: onec.p9; P1–P3; explicit contracts, types, collections and failure handling.
outcomes: Diagnose a defect using safe logs, a debugger and a reproducible scenario.
sections: Useful logs contain time, case/runID, operation and safe outcome. “Error” alone does not identify the stage or affected document. Use synthetic keys and no secrets. Correlation links request, handler and rejection without dumping a database publicly.

Engineering quality follows invariants, not absence of exceptions. Balance uses admissible amounts, permissions authorized scope, diagnostics explainable failure without leaks. Specify what survives errors and concurrent actions. Positive cases prove utility; negative cases prove boundaries. Denying everything is not a universally correct security implementation. Evidence needs both operational success and correctly bounded rejection.

Break at the expected branch, inspect types/values and step through. Editing variables is not evidence that the code is correct. Success after manual value injection is not a normal reproducible run. Record the first divergence and minimal inputs.

Transactions, locks and authorization solve different problems. Atomicity coordinates one operation, locking interacting operations, and rights constrain subjects. None proves the others. Identify decision point, read data and authorized actor for each failure scenario. Choose minimal protection rather than enabling every capability or broadening privileges. A context compile check is not a multi-user access proof.

Technical messages can include paths, queries and personal data. Keep raw logs private; share classifications and synthetic examples. Avoid hiding useful causes behind “try later,”but do not publish indiscriminately. Define log retention separately.

Measurement/observability must preserve privacy. Use synthetic IDs, bounded logs and defined metrics. Passwords/tokens are unnecessary even for leak demonstrations; use canaries. One timing is not p95, and one profile result does not cover every role/configuration combination. Keep raw diagnostics restricted and publish only sufficient sanitized evidence tied to the actual test environment.

Preserve failing case, hypothesis, attempt, outcome and cause. After fixing, repeat original and neighboring cases, including failure/preservation. If the issue disappears only under a debugger, investigate ordering/timing. Retain failed experiments to document boundaries and prevent repeating false paths.

Security acceptance needs discriminating tests in a permitted environment. Races need two controlled sessions, roles allowed work plus bypass attempts, and isolation denial of a specific resource. Preserve traces/post-failure state and repeat a successful control. Unsupported environments yieldNOTRUN; static analysis or diagrams cannot automatically fill that evidence gap. Report the remaining gate explicitly.

lab.title: Diagnose a defect using safe logs, a debugger and a reproducible scenario.
lab.environment: Official 1C 8.3.27.x, separate original teaching configuration and synthetic data. Metadata-dependent excerpts require the named objects; they are not standalone.os scripts. Full client-server/multi-user experiments need a separately permitted stand.
steps: Create a separate work copy; record its ID, source ID and platform/configuration build. Never restore over your source.
Reopen the copy, repeat the checks and reconcile the unchanged source. Preserve failures separately from the corrected attempt.
